Must issue the annual Fee-in-Lieu statement — none published Letter 5 Sheriff's Office 662-469-8500 County law enforcement, jail, civil process — Planning 662-469-8023 County zoning and land use outside city limits — Environmental Services 662-469-8152 Parks, greenways, environmental programmes — Source: DeSoto County published department directory, retrieved July 2026. Tax Collector satellite offices: Olive Branch 662-469-8032 , Horn Lake 662-469-8050 . State offices that matter here MDEQ Mississippi Dept. of Environmental Quality. Air permits, water withdrawal, environmental complaints. 601-961-5171 P.O. Box 2261, Jackson, MS 39225 Request the air permits → Mississippi Development Authority State incentives, data-centre certification, fee-in-lieu final approval. 601-359-3449 P.O. Box 849, Jackson, MS 39205-0849 Request the certification → Mississippi Ethics Commission Hears public-records complaints free of charge under § 25-61-13. Can order records released and fine an official who wrongfully withheld them. How to appeal a refusal → Mississippi State Auditor Takes citizen complaints about how public money is handled. Attach the records you received — or the letter refusing you. A documented complaint gets assigned. Get the documents first → Who publishes this page The Move Weight Foundation — not the City of Southaven and not DeSoto County. We are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit with no affiliation to either government, and nothing you submit to us reaches them unless you ask us to file it. We publish this directory because a resident should not need to know which of three governments handles their problem before they can get it fixed, and because the same office that answers your pothole call is the office that holds the records nobody has published. Those are the same phone number. That is the point. Every figure here is transcribed from an official published directory and dated. Governments reorganise and numbers change — if one is wrong, tell us and we will fix it and say when we did. For the City's own site, go to southaven.org ; for the County, desotocountyms.gov .

records.title: The documents
records.summary: Every record the City of Southaven released about xAI / MZX Tech, hosted in full and unaltered: the Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, the road MOU, the police donation, and four productions of water bills.
records.text: Document Library — every record, published whole | ExposeMississippi Skip to content Water Four productions of utility bills, plus the City's own explanation of how the meters work. 2026-05-22 Water Bills, production #4 27 pp The largest production and the source of the consumption figures on this site. Contains bills for two different customers : MZX Tech at 2875 Stanton (accounts 00014274 and 00014275 ) and GXO Supply Chain Inc at 2400 Stateline Rd W (accounts 00012324 / 00012326 ). Read the customer name on each bill before quoting a number — the two are easy to confuse and most of the pages are GXO's. Read the PDF ↓ Our transcription 2026-02-23 Email — the City's Billing Manager explains the water bills 2 pp Tina Hardy, Billing Manager of the Southaven Utilities Department, confirms there are three separate accounts for the single address , that the City bills a month behind, and that the unusual twelve-day first invoice exists because “there was already usage and an account had not been set up.” Short, plain, and the single most useful document for reading the meter data correctly. Read the PDF ↓ Where we quote it 2025-11-21 Water Bills, production #1 2 pp The earliest bills, on the original “2875 STANTON – POWER PLANT” account 00700460 : 14 CCF, then 132 CCF. The pre-construction baseline. Read the PDF ↓ 2026-02-05 Water Bills, production #2 5 pp The second production, following up on the first. Read the PDF ↓ 2026-02-23 Water Bills, production #3 6 pp The production that prompted the billing-manager email above. Read the PDF ↓ Permits, zoning and the neighbours What the City holds on how the site was approved and how it affects the people next to it. 2026-02-03 Zoning and NDAs Request 5 pp Requests zoning history and land-use classification for seven parcels — including 2875 Stanton Road S (Parcel 108522140 0000200) and 2400 Stateline Road W (108515000 0000700) — plus any parcel acquired or approved for xAI, MZX Tech LLC or affiliates since 1 January 2023, and any non-disclosure agreements. The parcel list is the best public map of the project's footprint. Read the PDF ↓ 2026-01-14 Sound Wall Request 3 pp Requests every noise permit, variance and exemption associated with the site from 1 August 2025, plus conditions, monitoring requirements, denials and enforcement records. The $12.8 million sound wall has been promised publicly; this asks whether anything about it exists on paper. Read the PDF ↓ 2026-01-14 Fire Department Permits 6 pp Fire Department permitting records for the site — relevant to fuel storage, generators, and the aqueous ammonia associated with turbine emissions control. Read the PDF ↓ Publication policy These documents are published whole. Nothing has been redacted, blurred, cropped, or edited. Every file is the City of Southaven's own production, byte for byte as it was released under the Mississippi Public Records Act. If a name, an address, a signature or a dollar figure appears in one of these files, it appears because the government put it in a public record and released it. That is the whole point. A transparency project that redacts the records it publishes is asking you to trust its judgment instead of showing you the evidence. We would rather you check our arithmetic than take our word for it. If you believe a document here contains something genuinely published in error by the City — not something merely inconvenient — tell us and we will look at it and say publicly what we decided.

records.title: They promised hundreds of jobs. The contract says twenty.
records.summary: The Governor promised hundreds of jobs. The signed contract requires twenty. A public-records project of the Move Weight Foundation covering xAI / MZX Tech in Southaven, Mississippi.
records.text: ExposeMississippi — The xAI deal in Southaven, in the city's own documents Skip to content Documented, promised, and still unanswered A promise is not a contract, and a contract is not a receipt. This site keeps the three apart on every page. Community fact sheets circulating in July listed the size and length of the tax break as secrets nobody outside the room knew. They are not secret. They are written in the agreement the City released, and they are reproduced below. Documented In a signed record you can read here 67% of ad valorem taxes abated — the fee is a stated one third of taxes otherwise payable Up to ten assessment years At least twenty new jobs — the only job number in the contract Binds future City and County boards , not just the ones that signed $6,690,900 paid or pledged to the City and its police department 16.5 million gallons of city water billed to MZX Tech in 132 days ? Promised Said in public; no signed paper compels it “Hundreds of permanent jobs” — no figure appears in the agreement $60 million a year to DeSoto County by 2028 $20 million a year to Southaven's general fund A $12.8 million sound wall New police, fire apparatus and roads — contingent on money arriving Unanswered What the released records do not show What the abatement is worth in dollars. No official has published the total Whether any board vote was ever taken in public on each payment Whether air permits exist for the turbines at the site What the schools receive under the apportionment Any clawback if the twenty jobs never appear How to close the gaps Every item in the third column is a public records request away. Mississippi gives a custodian seven working days to answer, and if they refuse, the Mississippi Ethics Commission hears the complaint for free and can order the records released. We will file it for you, or you can file it yourself → What they said, and what they signed Said in public “Hundreds of permanent jobs” No specific number was ever given. In the signed agreement “at least twenty (20) new jobs” Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, Recital B. No penalty is stated if even twenty never arrive. Said in public A $20 billion investment Announced January 2026. In the signed agreement “over $10 billion” Recital B. The contract's threshold is half the announced figure. Counted on the ground About 145 jobs so far The number community researchers can actually verify at the first building. In the signed agreement No penalty either way No released document requires repayment if the job numbers never arrive. Said in public The terms are confidential The size and length of the discount were described as unknown. In the signed agreement One third of taxes, ten years §§ 4 and 6, in the copy the City released. Read the clauses → Start here The Deal The Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, clause by clause: how much is abated, for how long, who is bound, and what xAI actually committed to. Read the agreement → The Payments $3.46M for roads, $1.85M from the Musk Foundation, $1,380,900 to the police department — and the dates they land relative to the tax vote. See the sequence → Water 16.5 million gallons billed to MZX Tech in 132 days, read straight off the City's own water bills, meter by meter. See the meter reads → Documents Every record the City has released, hosted in full, summarised in plain English, with the redaction log. Open the library → File a Records Request We file it as the Foundation so your name stays off it, and we publish whatever comes back. Seven working days by law. File a request → Anonymous Tip If you work for the City, the County, or on the site and something looks wrong, tell us. We do not log your address. Send a tip → Southaven is the first, not the last ExposeMississippi covers the whole state. Southaven is where it starts — because Southaven residents did the work first. The Safe and Sound Coalition filed the records requests that produced every document on this site, and DeSoto County is where the largest of these deals landed. That earns the first slot. Each city gets its own subdomain as it comes online, and Southaven's home is permanently southaven.exposemississippi.com — so nothing published today breaks when the next town is added. Until then the front door lands here. Another Mississippi town, same playbook? Abatement negotiated behind closed doors, promises with no signed paper behind them, records requests that go unanswered — if that is happening where you live, tell us . The method on this site travels: the statute, the seven-working-day clock and the free Ethics Commission appeal are the same in all 82 counties. Get the next document when it lands One email when a request comes back or a new record is published. Nothing else, ever. Notify me The Move Weight Foundation is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit. We are not affiliated with the City of Southaven, DeSoto County, the State of Mississippi, xAI, or MZX Tech, LLC.

records.title: Who signed what
records.summary: The officials who signed, approved or administer the xAI agreements in Southaven and DeSoto County, and the campaign finance records the Foundation has requested for each.
records.text: Officials — who signed what | ExposeMississippi Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Southaven, MS of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Accountability Who signed what Names appear here because a person's official signature, vote or statutory duty is attached to one of these documents. This is a record of responsibility, not an accusation against anyone. City of Southaven Official Role Connection to the record Campaign finance Darren Musselwhite Mayor Signed the $1,380,900 Donation Agreement for the Police Department on 10 Feb 2026. A party to the Ad Valorem Tax Agreement through the Mayor and Board of Aldermen. Requested Board of Aldermen Governing board The “City Board” under the tax agreement. Individual votes on the MOU, the grant, the donation and the abatement are not in the released records. Requested City Clerk Records custodian Holds the agendas, minutes and resolutions. Municipal campaign finance reports are also filed here. — Tina Hardy Billing Manager, Utilities Explained the three water accounts at 2875 Stanton in writing. Named only because her explanation is quoted and readers should know its source. — DeSoto County Official Role Connection to the record Campaign finance Jessie Medlin President, Board of Supervisors The County Board is a “Granting Authority” under the tax agreement. Requested Board of Supervisors Governing board Each member who voted on the Fee-in-Lieu agreement in January 2026. Requested Jeff Fitch Tax Assessor A named party. Sets the valuation and depreciation that determine the fee under Exhibit B § 1(b)(iv). Requested Joey Treadway Tax Collector A named party. Must issue the annual written statement of the Fee-in-Lieu Amount under Exhibit B § 2(a). None has been published. Requested State of Mississippi Body Role Connection to the record Status Mississippi Development Authority State economic development Certified the project and executed the Certificate of Final Approval (Exhibit A) under Miss. Code Ann. § 27-31-104(3), on or about 24 Feb 2026. Also administers the sales and use tax exemption under § 57-113-21. Requested Mississippi Dept. of Environmental Quality Environmental regulator Holds the air permitting record for 2875 Stanton Road S — the question of whether turbines are operating with or without permits sits here. Requested Mississippi Ethics Commission Records appeal authority Not involved in the deal. Named because it is where a denied records request is appealed, free of charge, under § 25-61-13. How to appeal On campaign finance The Foundation has prepared requests for the 2024–2026 campaign finance disclosures of every official above who signed or voted, with itemised contribution schedules, addressed to the DeSoto County Circuit Clerk, the Southaven City Clerk, and the Secretary of State's Elections Division. What “requested” means, and what it does not It means a records request exists. It does not mean any contribution has been found, and it is not a suggestion that any official has done anything wrong. When the filings arrive we will publish them in full, including the ones that show nothing. A transparency project that only publishes the damaging half of what it receives is not a transparency project. File a campaign finance request → Read the documents

records.title: File a public records request
records.summary: File a Mississippi Public Records Act request through the Move Weight Foundation. Seven working days by law, free appeal to the Ethics Commission, and ready-to-send letter templates for Southaven and DeSoto County.
records.text: File a Mississippi Public Records Request | ExposeMississippi Skip to content Ready-to-send letter templates Five requests drafted for this specific project, covering the environmental, financial and political record. Download, add your name, and send — or use the form above and we will send it for you. Each letter stands alone and goes to a different office. Letter 1 MDEQ — air permits at 2875 Stanton Road S 2 pp Permit applications, exemption claims for stationary combustion turbines, correspondence with the company and its consultants, inspection and violation records, and aqueous ammonia / SCR records. Written to settle one question: are the turbines running with air permits or without them? Download PDF ↓ Letter 2 City of Southaven — board minutes and resolutions 2 pp Agendas, minutes, resolutions and vote tallies for all four instruments; executive-session certifications; records of receipt and expenditure of the $3.46M, $1.85M and $1,380,900; and legal advice on whether the City could accept a grant carrying a confidentiality clause. Download PDF ↓ Letter 3 Mississippi Development Authority — certification & compliance 2 pp The full data-centre certification application under § 57-113-21, the job and wage thresholds MDA applied, every compliance report and clawback analysis, and the Certificate of Final Approval. This is where a job commitment would be, if one exists. Download PDF ↓ Letter 4 Campaign finance — Circuit Clerk, City Clerk, Secretary of State 2 pp 2024–2026 disclosure reports with itemised contribution schedules for the officials who signed or voted on these agreements. Includes companion paragraphs for the City Clerk (municipal filings) and the Secretary of State (statewide committees). Download PDF ↓ Letter 5 DeSoto County Tax Assessor & Collector — the FIL arithmetic 2 pp Personal property renditions, valuations and depreciation schedules, and every annual written statement of the Fee-in-Lieu Amount required by Exhibit B § 2(a) — with the underlying calculation and the “Taxes Otherwise Payable” figure. This is the request that would finally show what the abatement costs. Download PDF ↓ Filing notes The City of Southaven uses its own Public Record Request form — you may attach Letter 2 to it. MDEQ takes both an online portal and mail; sending both is fastest. Municipal officials file campaign finance with the City Clerk, county officials with the Circuit Clerk, statewide committees with the Secretary of State. None of this is legal advice; these are records requests any citizen may file. Records custodian directory Who holds what, and how each office accepts a request. records.title: Watching Mississippi, one county at a time
records.summary: The Move Weight Foundation
records.text: ExposeMississippi — public records across Mississippi | ExposeMississippi Skip to content The expansion queue Places we intend to cover next. These are not accusations. Each is on the list because of its structure — a large capital project, a dominant employer, fast growth, or a big incentive package — which is where public money concentrates and where the documents are worth reading. If something is wrong there, the records will show it. If nothing is wrong, the records will show that too, and we will publish it either way. DeSoto County (beyond Southaven) Olive Branch, Horn Lake and Hernando sit on the same tax base and the same aquifer. Know something here? → Jackson & Hinds County The capital's water system is under federal oversight; the contracting record is public. Know something here? → Gulfport & Biloxi Harrison County. Post-disaster recovery funds and casino-adjacent development agreements. Know something here? → Madison & Rankin Counties The fastest-growing suburbs in the state, with matching infrastructure commitments. Know something here? → Tupelo & Lee County Long-running industrial recruitment and fee-in-lieu agreements of the same shape as Southaven's. Know something here? → Your town not listed? The queue is not a ranking and it is not fixed. A resident who knows what to ask for beats our guess about which county matters every time. Tell us what is happening where you live → You do not have to wait for us Mississippi's public records law covers every city, county, school district and state agency — not just the ones we have built a site for. The request we would file on your behalf is one you can file yourself today, and we will help you write it. Name a document, not a topic. “All agendas and minutes referencing X between these two dates” is hard to refuse. “Everything about X” invites a denial for being overly broad. Put the deadline in the letter. Citing the statute tells the custodian you know the clock is running. Ask for the exemption in writing. If they withhold, they must say which provision lets them. Escalate on paper. A refusal that exists in writing is the beginning of an appeal, not the end of a request. Use our request builder → About the Foundation

records.title: The Deal
records.summary: xAI
records.text: The Deal — the Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, clause by clause | ExposeMississippi Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Southaven, MS of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → The Ad Valorem Tax Agreement · Effective 6 January 2026 The Deal This is the contract that abates xAI's property taxes in Southaven and DeSoto County. The City released it. Below is what each operative clause actually says, quoted verbatim, with our plain-English reading beside it. Who signed it This Ad Valorem Tax Agreement (the “Agreement”) is made and entered into as of January 6, 2026 (the “Effective Date”), by and among: DeSoto County, Mississippi… the City of Southaven, Mississippi… the Tax Assessor of DeSoto County… the Tax Collector of DeSoto County… and MZX Tech, LLC , its successors and assigns (the “Company”)… The Mississippi Development Authority (“MDA”) joins this Agreement through its execution of the Certificate of Final Approval attached as Exhibit “A”. Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, p. 1 · source document Six parties. The City and the County are the “Granting Authorities.” The County Tax Assessor and Tax Collector are added because they are the offices that will have to bill a reduced amount every year for a decade. MZX Tech, LLC is xAI's entity; the same name appears on the police donation and on the water bills. What xAI actually committed to B. The Project is anticipated to involve a capital investment of over $10 billion and to create at least twenty (20) new jobs . Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, Recital B · source document This is the only job figure anywhere in the agreement. Public statements described “hundreds of permanent jobs” and a $20 billion investment. The binding document sets the bar at twenty jobs and ten billion dollars . Note the verb. The project is “anticipated to involve” that investment — recitals describe expectations, they are not covenants. The operative conditions on the abatement, in § 3, are the Minimum Capital Investment and MDA approval. Job creation is not among them. What this means Nothing in the released agreement requires xAI to hire anyone in order to keep the tax break, and nothing in it makes the company repay a dollar if the jobs never appear. If a clawback exists, it is in a document that has not been released. That is a records request → How much is abated 6. Amount of Fee-in-Lieu. The FIL Amount payable for each Assessment Year of the FIL Term shall be a stated one-third (1/3) of the Taxes Otherwise Payable by the Company… Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, § 6, p. 5 · source document A “fee in lieu” replaces the property tax bill with a smaller fee. Here the fee is one third of what would otherwise be owed — so two thirds of the property tax is abated , every year, for the whole term. 5. Scope of Abatement. The Fee-in-Lieu granted herein shall abate and be in lieu of all Taxes Otherwise Payable and the obligation to make the FIL Payment shall be in lieu of the obligation to pay Taxes Otherwise Payable. Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, § 5, p. 5 “All” is doing real work in that sentence. This is not a discount on one parcel; it replaces the entire ad valorem obligation on the project's property with the reduced fee. For how long, and on what 4. Property Subject to Fee-in-Lieu. All Property installed or subject to appraisal by the Tax Assessor or otherwise subject to ad valorem taxation prior to or during the FIL Term… shall be included in and subject to the Fee-in-Lieu for a period of up to ten (10) Assessment Years … specifically including Property owned by or taxable to Additional Participants, whether acquired before or during the FIL Term. Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, § 4, p. 5 Two things worth noticing. First, ten years . Second, the abatement reaches “Additional Participants” — other companies that join the project later can be swept under the same discount without a fresh public negotiation. § 21 (Assignability) governs how they are added, and lessors are pulled in automatically under Miss. Code Ann. § 27-31-104(1)(b). Whether a future board can undo it b. Binding Commitments. Pursuant to MCA §§ 27-31-104(4) and 27-31-107, this Agreement constitutes a binding obligation of each Party (including future County Boards and City Boards) upon execution by the Granting Authorities and the Company and approval by MDA up to and through the FIL Term… Ad Valorem Tax Agreement, § 3.b, p. 5 The boards that signed in January 2026 bound every board that follows them for the length of the term. Voters who elect a different Board of Aldermen or Board of Supervisors cannot instruct their new representatives to reopen this agreement. Who checks the arithmetic The agreement leaves the annual number in the hands of two county offices. Exhibit B § 2(a) requires the Tax Collector to issue a written statement of the FIL Amount each year. Exhibit B § 1(b)(iv) allows discretionary reductions for obsolescence and accelerated depreciation — meaning the taxable value of the equipment, and therefore the fee, can fall faster than the equipment wears out. Section 10 apportions whatever is collected among the local school district, the City and the County. None of those annual statements has been published. Until they are, nobody outside those offices can say what Southaven's schools actually receive. Requested The Foundation has prepared a records request to the DeSoto County Tax Assessor and Tax Collector for every rendition, valuation, depreciation schedule and annual FIL statement. Use the same template yourself → What we are not saying A tax abatement is legal in Mississippi. Miss. Code Ann. § 27-31-104 exists precisely to let local governments grant one, and the Mississippi Development Authority approved this one. Publishing the terms is not an accusation that anybody broke a law. What we are saying is narrower and harder to argue with: the public was given one set of numbers and the contract contains another, the contract binds boards that have not been elected yet, and the documents that would show what it costs have not been released. Those are facts about paperwork, and they are fixable by producing the paperwork. Next: the payments → Read the full agreement

records.title: The Payments
records.summary: $3.46M for roads, $1.85M from the Musk Foundation, $1,380,900 to the Southaven Police Department, and a tax agreement effective in between. The dates, from the signed records.
records.text: The Payments — $6.69 million, and when it moved | ExposeMississippi Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Southaven, MS of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Three agreements · December 2025 – February 2026 The Payments In the ten weeks around the tax agreement, MZX Tech and the Musk Foundation put $6,690,900 in front of the City of Southaven. Here is each payment, what document created it, and when it was signed. The sequence Dates below are taken from the face of each document. We present them in order and without commentary about motive, because the order is the fact and motive is not something a contract can show. 23 December 2025 Memorandum of Understanding — $3,460,000 roads MZX Tech, LLC and the City agree on $3,460,000 for improvements to Stateline Road and Tulane Road — the roads serving the site. MOU for Stateline Rd, released by the City 29 December 2025 Musk Foundation Grant Agreement — $1,850,000 A grant to the City from the Musk Foundation. The agreement contains a confidentiality provision at Section 6 . Whether a Mississippi municipality can accept a grant conditioned on confidentiality, consistent with the Public Records Act, is a question the City's outside counsel would have had to consider. Identified in the City's own records index · requested in full 6 January 2026 Ad Valorem Tax Agreement takes effect 67% abated, 10 years The fee-in-lieu agreement's stated Effective Date. Two thirds of the project's property taxes are abated for up to ten assessment years, binding on future boards. The Board of Aldermen met that night. We pulled the City's published agenda for 6 January 2026 and read all eighteen items. Here is what it shows. The agreement, clause by clause · the agenda in full 10 February 2026 Donation Agreement — $1,380,900 to the Police Department MZX Tech LLC donates $1,380,900 to the City of Southaven for the exclusive use of the Southaven Police Department. Signed by Mayor Darren Musselwhite on 2–10–2026. SPD Donation Agreement, released by the City 24 February 2026 MDA Certificate of Final Approval executed The Mississippi Development Authority's Executive Director signs the certificate that makes the fee-in-lieu final under Miss. Code Ann. § 27-31-104(3). Exhibit A to the tax agreement · full application requested from MDA What the agenda for 6 January 2026 shows The Ad Valorem Tax Agreement states its Effective Date as 6 January 2026. The Mayor and Board of Aldermen met at 6:00 PM that evening. The City published the agenda. We host it in full ; these four items are quoted from it verbatim. 6. Resolution for Emergency Expenditure for Traffic Signal at Intersection of Tulane Rd. and Stateline Rd. 13. Citizen’s Agenda: Jason Haley, Shannon Samsa 18. Executive Session: Economic Development (Potential Location of Business/Industry to City); Interdepartmental Personnel with No Action Meeting of the Mayor and Board of Aldermen, Southaven, Mississippi · 6 January 2026, 6:00 PM · source PDF Four observations, and one thing we cannot tell you No public item names the tax agreement. Across all eighteen items, nothing on the published agenda mentions MZX Tech, xAI, “Project Synergy,” ad valorem tax, or a fee-in-lieu — on the day the agreement took effect. Item 18 closed the meeting for economic development. The stated purpose is “Potential Location of Business/Industry to City.” Mississippi permits an executive session for that purpose, and closing one is not by itself improper. What it means here is that the public record of that evening stops at the door. Item 6 is Tulane and Stateline. Those are the two roads named in the $3,460,000 MOU with MZX Tech signed fourteen days earlier, now appearing as an emergency traffic-signal expenditure. Item 13 is two residents on the citizen’s agenda — Jason Haley and Shannon Samsa, the Vice Director and Director of the Safe and Sound Coalition . They put themselves on the record that night. What we cannot tell you, and why An agenda proves an item was scheduled . It does not show what was decided, how anyone voted, or what was said behind a closed door. The minutes for this meeting have not been published — the City's agenda portal carries agendas only. So we are not saying the abatement was approved in secret. We are saying the public record of 6 January 2026 does not show it being approved in public, and the document that would settle it is a records request away. Mississippi also requires a certification of the reason for any executive session — that is a public record too. Both are in the template we have prepared → The police donation, in its own words 1. Donation. The Donor agrees to donate the sum of $1,380,900 (the “Donation”) to the Recipient. Recipient agrees to use the Donation exclusively for The City of Southaven Police Department and in accordance with applicable Mississippi laws. 2. No Quid Pro Quo. This Donation is made without any expectation of goods, services, or benefits in return , other than any applicable tax deductions for the Donor under federal and state law, if any. Donation Agreement, §§ 1–2 · source document The donor is MZX Tech LLC, of 1450 Page Mill Road, Palo Alto, California . The recipient is the City. The agreement is governed by Mississippi law and states that it supersedes any prior agreements between the parties. Two things on the face of the released copy The donor never signed it. On the copy the City released, the DONOR signature block — signature, printed name, title and date — is blank . Only the City executed the document, on 10 February 2026. § 3 anticipates a vote that the released records do not show. The City “confirms that acceptance of the Donation complies with Mississippi municipal laws and has been (or will be) formally approved [e.g., city council resolution] to the extent required.” No minutes or resolution recording that approval has been released. An unsigned counterpart is not by itself evidence of anything improper — parties often sign in counterparts and produce only one. We note it because the released record is the record, and this is what it shows. If a fully executed copy exists, producing it settles the point in a single email. Where the money went Date Instrument Payer Amount Stated purpose 2025-12-23 Memorandum of Understanding MZX Tech, LLC $3,460,000 Stateline Rd & Tulane Rd improvements 2025-12-29 Grant Agreement Musk Foundation $1,850,000 Not stated in released records 2026-02-10 Donation Agreement MZX Tech, LLC $1,380,900 Southaven Police Department Total $6,690,900 Still unanswered Which fund each payment was deposited into, what has been spent from it, whether each was accepted by a recorded vote on a published agenda, and what legal advice the City took on the Musk Foundation grant's confidentiality clause. All of it is requestable, and all of it is in the letter the Foundation has prepared for the City Clerk. Use the template → Next: the water → Read the documents

The Board of Aldermen minutes or resolution accepting the $1,380,900 police donation, the $1.85M grant, or the $3.46M road MOU. The fully executed copy of the Donation Agreement — the released version is unsigned by the donor. Any annual Fee-in-Lieu statement issued by the DeSoto County Tax Collector under Exhibit B § 2(a). Any clawback, job-verification or compliance report filed with the MDA. Any water supply agreement , well permit, or withdrawal report for the site. The Musk Foundation grant agreement , particularly its Section 6 confidentiality clause and any legal advice the City took on it. You do not need to have a document in hand. Knowing what something is called and which office holds it is often enough for us to go and get it.

records.summary: Where to watch Southaven government on video — meeting recordings, agendas, and the archives that keep them after the city takes them down.
records.text: Watch your government | ExposeMississippi Skip to content MW A chapter of the Move Weight Foundation Southaven, MS of 14 Oklahoma 4 Miami Oklahoma City Tulsa Claremore Texas 7 San Angelo Houston Dallas Austin San Antonio Lubbock Abilene Mississippi 3 Southaven Jackson Olive Branch All 14 chapters and the map → Video · Southaven, MS Watch your government Almost every decision that costs you money is made in a room with a camera in it. The recordings are public. Most people never find them because they are buried three clicks deep on a government site. Here they are. Where the video lives Southaven uploads Board of Aldermen video usually within an hour of the meeting ending. These are the City's own recordings — we link to them, we do not rehost them. Board of Aldermen meetings City of Southaven Agendas, minutes, packets and meeting video. 1st & 3rd Tuesday, 6:00 p.m. Open → City of Southaven — Board Meetings City of Southaven The City's official channel. Meetings stream live 1st and 3rd Tuesday at 6pm and stay up afterwards. Open → Safe and Sound Coalition Community Resident-recorded footage and documentation of the plant and its noise. Open → We link, we do not rehost These are the government's own recordings on the government's own platforms. We send you there rather than mirroring them, so you are watching the authoritative copy and the view count lands where it belongs. The exception is when a recording disappears — see below. When a recording goes missing Meeting video gets taken down. Sometimes it is a retention policy, sometimes a platform migration, sometimes nobody can say why. Either way the public record evaporates, and the one meeting you needed is the one that is gone. That is why the Foundation's Miami, Oklahoma chapter keeps 522 meetings archived with machine transcripts and captions , mirrored to the Internet Archive. It is the deepest archive we run and the model for every other chapter. See what a full archive looks like → If you spot a gap A meeting with no video, a recording that ends mid-item, a link that used to work — tell us . A missing recording is itself a records request: the city holds the raw file whether or not it publishes it, and we will ask for it. Getting more out of a meeting recording Read the agenda packet first. It usually contains the actual contract or ordinance. The video is people discussing a document you can already have in front of you. Note the timestamp of anything that matters. A citation like "14 January, 1:42:10" is something a reporter or an auditor can verify in a minute. Watch the vote, not the speech. Who moved it, who seconded, who was absent, and whether it was on a published agenda. Executive session is a flag, not a crime. Bodies may close a meeting for defined reasons and must certify which. If a payment or a contract was discussed behind a closed door, the certification is a public record. Ask for it → Follow this chapter No social accounts yet. When the Foundation creates one for this chapter it is added to chapters/mississippi.json and appears here and in the footer automatically. We publish to the site first. Social accounts are a distribution channel, never the record — anything we post there exists here with its source document attached.

records.title: 16.5 million gallons in 132 days
records.summary: MZX Tech was billed for 16,541,674 gallons of Southaven city water in 132 days. Every meter read transcribed from the water bills the City released.
records.text: Water — 16.5 million gallons, read off the city's own bills | ExposeMississippi Skip to content The household comparison uses the common US figure of roughly 300 gallons per household per day. The peak figure is the first billed period: 10,392 CCF over twelve days. About that first bill — the City explained it in writing The 25 November – 7 December bill shows a previous read of zero and covers only twelve days. Asked about it, the City of Southaven's Utilities Department Billing Manager answered directly: We bill a month behind. The first bills usually either a small amount of days or longer than 30 days… This one only had 12 days so we could get the account started billing since there was already usage and an account had not been set up for that account . There are three different accounts for this one address.. 00014274 — 00014275 — 00700460 Tina Hardy, Billing Manager, City of Southaven Utilities Department, 23 February 2026 · source email So the 10,392 CCF is not twelve days of use. By the City's own account it is consumption that had already occurred before a billing account existed for it , caught up in the first invoice. The four full monthly periods that follow are unambiguous and average 2,930 CCF — about 2.2 million gallons a month. Before the data center The same customer number, on the older account 00700460 (“2875 STANTON – POWER PLANT”), shows what the site used before construction ramped: Read period CCF used Gallons Charged 18 Aug – 08 Sep 2025 14 10,473 $154.00 08 Sep – 08 Oct 2025 132 98,743 $508.20 Fourteen CCF in three weeks, then 132 in a month. Ten weeks later the new account was billing 10,392 . A second meter at 2875 Stanton Rd, account 00014275 , registered 192 CCF in December 2025 and has read flat at 192 — zero use — on every bill since. What we checked, and one thing we nearly got wrong The City's water-bill productions are scans. Machine-read text from them is unreliable, so every figure on this page was transcribed by eye from the bill image, and every bill was checked for who it is addressed to before any number was used. Correction we caught before publishing Most of the bills in the fourth production are not MZX Tech's. They are billed to GXO Supply Chain Inc at 2400 Stateline Rd W — a different company, on different accounts ( 00012324 / 00012326 , customer 84062 ). Their usage appears nowhere in our totals. If you see figures such as 938, 706 or 259 CCF attributed to xAI anywhere, they are GXO's meter, not xAI's. 2400 Stateline Rd W does appear in the Foundation's request to the DeSoto County Tax Assessor as a project-related property, so the address matters — but the water account there belongs to another business, and we will not blur the two. What the bills cannot tell you Southaven's water comes from the Memphis Sand aquifer , the same groundwater the whole region draws on. Metered municipal consumption is only part of a data center's water picture: a site may also hold its own permitted wells, recycle cooling water, or draw surface water, and none of that appears on a city utility bill. So this page reports exactly what it can prove — the water the City sold and billed — and nothing beyond it. The rest requires records the Foundation has requested: well permits and withdrawal reporting from MDEQ, and any water-supply agreement between the City and the company. One more thing on these bills Every bill charges 7% sales tax on the water — $5,959.45 across the five periods. The state waived sales tax on the data center's computing equipment. It did not waive it on the water. Request the well permits → See the source bills
